papers.title: Symmetry classification of hyperfine rovibrational molecular phase space
papers.abstract: Symmetry-based structures have advanced molecular spectroscopy and quantum information science, yet connections between these fields remain largely unexplored. We construct a phase space theory of a molecule by jointly treating rotational, vibrational, and nuclear-spin degrees of freedom as the quotient of orientations and normal coordinates by the molecule's point group. The various combinations of how these three degrees of freedom transform under symmetries organize a molecule's states into molecular species, and we show that each species is defined by a particular absolutely maximally entangled (AME) carrier state, or, for 45 species, by a two-dimensional space of them. Up to local unitaries and the order of the sectors, molecular species realize 21 AME states across 75 point groups: a product state, four maximally entangled pairs, and 16 genuinely tripartite states. A Fourier transform on the quotient relates orientation and angular-momentum descriptions while preserving these carrier states. We propose an example experimental protocol for preparing and driving symmetry-adapted bend states of $\mathrm{CaOCH_3}$.

papers.title: Enhancement of Weak Interactions in Phase Transitions in Condensed Matter and Early Universe
papers.abstract: Parity-violating weak interactions produce extremely small energy differences between left- and right-handed chiral systems. We show that these microscopic effects may be amplified during collective phenomena such as phase transitions. The enhancement factor is proportional to the critical number of atoms, $N_c$, in the nucleus of the new phase. Measurement of the ratio of produced left- and right-handed chiral structures may provide a way to determine $N_c$. Experiments in which spin-chiral structures are formed in ZnCr$_2$Se$_4$ during a phase transition in crossed electric and magnetic fields indicate an effective amplification corresponding to $N_c\sim 10^9-10^{10}$. We emphasize, however, that such large values cannot be inferred from homogeneous capillary nucleation alone, since the same parameters imply a very large nucleation barrier; in real crystals heterogeneous nucleation, defects, strain, and domain-growth dynamics may be essential. We also discuss, more cautiously, whether analogous collective enhancement could operate in first-order cosmological phase transitions beyond the Standard Model. The Standard-Model electroweak transition for the observed Higgs mass is a crossover and therefore has no critical bubble nucleus.

papers.title: Rabi-Engineered spin-selective transport of bright soliton in a binary spin-1/2 condensate
papers.abstract: Spintronics is usually concentrated on spin-dependent dynamics of single particles such as electrons or holes in solids. Extending this concept to nonlinear matter waves offers an interesting possibility of controlling the transport of collective, particle-like excitations through their spin degrees of freedom. Recent advances in Bose-Einstein condensates have provided a versatile platform for realizing nonlinear spin-1/2 systems that support particle-like objects such as bright solitons, making studies of the motion of these solitons under external fields an interesting and important problem. Here, we study the dynamics of bright solitons with different spin symmetries moving in a coordinate-dependent Rabi field, which acts analogously to a spatially varying magnetic field. In that setup, the velocity perturbed soliton motion possesses very interesting scattering dynamics for both perfect and lifted Manakov symmetry. Lastly, we compare both the velocity-controlled scattering problem with the well-known Rabi quenching protocol. This comparison provides a powerful approach to control the soliton dynamics that may open an avenue to control nonlinear spintronics with solitons as spin carriers.

papers.title: Sub-Doppler Cooling of Potassium-41 in a Hybrid Quadrupole-Octupole Symmetry Magneto-Optical Trap
papers.abstract: Sub-Doppler cooling processes rely on the near-degeneracy of the Zeeman sub-levels of the atom. Effective sub-Doppler cooling is only achieved when the ac-Stark shift of the molasses light is significantly larger than the Zeeman shift. This condition is typically achieved by switching off all magnetic gradients, and using Helmholtz coils to cancel Earth's magnetic field. Another way to achieve a nearly zero magnetic field gradient is to superimpose a second pair of oppositely oriented quadrupole coils with a different spatial geometry. At the ideal current ratio, this creates an octupole-symmetry magnetic field for the atoms. The resulting octupole magnetic field has a gradient increasing quadratically from zero at the center. In this work, the effectiveness of sub-Doppler cooling and trapping using D2 and D1 light is evaluated in such a hybrid trap for $^{41}$K. The temperature, lifetime, and phase-space density of the atoms are measured. For both D2 and D1 light, the octupole MOT is found to have a longer lifetime, while maintaining a similar temperature to the zero-field case. D1 gray-molasses temperatures down to $3.8(1)~\mu$K and phase-space density up to $5.3(4)\times10^{-5}$ are measured for $14.3(1)\times10^6$ $^{41}$ atoms. The effectiveness of the hybrid quadrupole-octupole trap suggests the possibility of increasing the loading time for atoms into an optical dipole trap with active sub-Doppler cooling.

papers.title: Probing the Nuclear E2 Transition Amplitude in $^{229}$Th via Quantum Interference
papers.abstract: The nuclear E2 transition amplitude of $^{229}$Th probes nuclear deformation and configuration mixing, yet remains poorly constrained by measurements dominated by M1 radiation. We propose to determine its magnitude and sign relative to the nuclear M1 transition amplitude through quantum interference in $^{229}$Th$^{3+}$. Two coherent laser fields couple a superposition of initial hyperfine states to a common nuclear isomeric state through the electronic shell. Varying the mixing angle controls interference between the excitation pathways, allowing the signed E2/M1 transition amplitude ratio to be extracted using the calibrated laser-field amplitude ratio, without absolute intensity calibration. An independent M1 reference then determines the E2 magnitude. Dynamical calculations support the feasibility of the scheme, predicting appreciable nuclear excitation with milliwatt laser power on millisecond timescales. We evaluate the extraction sensitivity to experimental and atomic-structure uncertainties. The approach extends to other $^{229}$Th ions, whose rich level structures offer a broader selection of transitions and promising routes to suppress systematic uncertainties.

papers.title: Quantum Mpemba effect in a driven-dissipative atom-waveguide coupled system
papers.abstract: The quantum Mpemba effect (QME) describes the counterintuitive phenomenon in which a more strongly perturbed quantum system relaxes toward its steady state faster than a less perturbed one. Here, we investigate the QME in a weakly driven-dissipative atomic array coupled to a one-dimensional chiral waveguide. Starting from the steady state, we introduce a local quench by resetting a single atom to its ground state and examine the subsequent relaxation dynamics. We find that quenching atoms near the array boundaries induces faster initial relaxation through enhanced coupling to superradiant modes and direct photon emission into the waveguide, giving rise to an edge-enhanced QME. Strong directional decay further amplifies this effect by promoting the spatial accumulation of superradiant modes near the preferred boundary, leading to a skin-enhanced QME. At later times, relaxation is increasingly governed by long-lived subradiant modes localized predominantly in the bulk of the array. By coupling two atomic arrays with different interparticle spacings, we further demonstrate an interface-induced QME, where quenching an atom near the interface makes the system relax more slowly at early times but approach its steady state faster at later times, owing to weak participation in both superradiant and subradiant modes. Our findings reveal how the spatial structure of collective decay modes and directional dissipation jointly govern anomalous quantum relaxation, offering potential routes toward accelerated steady-state preparation in waveguide QED systems.

papers.title: Squeezed Cooling and Lasing with Cold Atoms in Cavity-QED
papers.abstract: A squeezed laser undergoes a lasing transition into a squeezed cavity mode, where stimulated emission generates a bright coherent field with a laser-like coherence time while maintaining one field quadrature below the vacuum noise level. Here we propose an optical implementation that needs neither a nonlinear crystal nor injected squeezed light, based on engineered interactions between ensembles of rubidium atoms and a squeezed cavity mode via cavity-assisted Raman transitions. A first ensemble cools the cavity into a squeezed vacuum, a mechanism we term squeezed cooling, yielding up to 9 dB in the intracavity field, surpassing the 3 dB limit of optical parametric oscillators. Tuned for output instead, it reaches up to 18 dB of output squeezing. Incoherently pumping a second ensemble drives a lasing transition into the squeezed mode, emitting a bright beam with long coherence time and noise below vacuum spanning a megahertz-wide band, away from the sharp phase-diffusion peak of excess noise at the carrier frequency, and robust to relaxation oscillations. We characterize lasing thresholds, superradiant emission, and linewidth narrowing, and identify the experimentally accessible regime where the system exhibits the defining features of a squeezed laser.

papers.title: Residual Allan Stability under Periodic Auxiliary Ramsey Sampling
papers.abstract: The timing of auxiliary Ramsey measurements can change the frequency stability associated with a drifting pulse shift at a fixed nominal Fisher-information rate for a constant shift. For periodic instantaneous observations of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck shift with causal prediction between updates, we derive the exact residual covariance averaged over the update cycle and the corresponding Allan variance at arbitrary averaging times. Relative to a continuous Kalman reference at the same information rate, periodic estimation increases the cycle-averaged estimation-error variance, reduces the short-time residual Allan variance, and increases its long-time value. Its covariance decays more slowly at the origin and has a larger integral. We extend the result to instantaneous sensing of the sum of finitely many independent Ornstein-Uhlenbeck modes. Integrated observations preserve the short-time ordering for the scalar shift, and numerical calculations resolve the dependence of the crossover on window duration. A zero-order-hold comparison shows that the short-time ordering can change when the same estimator drives a different correction command. A three-level Ramsey model of coherent population trapping (CPT) maps the discriminator response to an effective information budget and illustrates how the dark times affect the choice of schedule.

papers.title: Attosecond soft X-ray pulses generated by chirp-dispersed manipulation in an XFEL reveal nonlinear core-electron dynamics in neon
papers.abstract: Free-electron lasers deliver intense attosecond X-ray pulses, which are the key to studying electron dynamics in specifically targeted electronic states, but come at the expense of complicated generation schemes and stochastic pulse shapes. Here, we demonstrate a novel and simple operation concept based on dispersive manipulation of the lasing electron bunch and capable of working with the full 4.5 MHz repetition rate at the European XFEL in Germany. Using a high-fidelity single-shot temporal characterisation, we detect X-ray pulses with durations of down to 200 attoseconds and peak powers reaching into the terawatt regime at ~1 keV photon energy. As a direct application, we present simultaneous measurements of nonlinear X-ray-matter interaction via time-resolved electron spectroscopy. Using the pulse duration retrieval and restricting the durations to a regime where individual X-ray pulses are shorter than the single-core-hole life time in neon atoms, we reveal an otherwise hidden peak-intensity dependence in the nonlinear dynamics of double-core-hole formation. Our results shed light on highly transient intermediate steps in complex electronic dynamics of systems driven far off their equilibrium state, and thus promise to help build the conceptual bridge between fundamental physics processes and real-world photo reactions.

papers.title: Transversal surface-code game with reconfigurable qubits
papers.abstract: Qubit platforms supporting flexible connectivity have opened the door to theoretical advances in fault-tolerant quantum computation (FTQC), offering a compelling alternative to lattice surgery by leveraging transversal gates. Among such systems, neutral atoms have demonstrated notable progress enabled by large-scale parallel atom transport. However, a crucial gap remains between the theory of FTQC and its practical realization with these systems. Most critically, a key theoretical requirement, that syndrome extraction must be performed frequently enough to keep error accumulation below a threshold constant, is not satisfied in a scalable manner in the existing approach due to increased transport times. In this work, we develop a theoretical framework that closes such a gap, bridging theoretical advances in fault-tolerant protocols with the latest experimental capabilities. Building on the "game of surface code" framework originally developed for superconducting qubits, we introduce an alternative game-based paradigm for transversal-gate FTQC, formulating the protocol as a transversal surface-code game governed by rules for mode transitions of code cells. The rulesets are designed to enable syndrome extraction at any intermediate step during logical gate implementation, ensuring compatibility with the threshold theorem, while fully exploiting the capabilities of the hardware to scale and accelerate FTQC. As an application, our framework offers a systematic methodology and high-level abstraction for resource estimation and optimization; an exemplary estimation for a neutral-atom system demonstrates performance competitive with a baseline lattice-surgery-based approach on superconducting qubits, even with physical operations orders of magnitude slower. These results bridge the theory and experiment of FTQC with reconfigurable qubits toward scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computers.

papers.title: UNWRAP: Single-shot phase analysis of bright squeezed vacuum by Newton-ring interferometry
papers.abstract: The mean field of pulsed bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) vanishes, but the variance can be large, and is strongly phase-dependent. We employ ultrafast Newton-ring wavefront retrieval and analysis of phase (UNWRAP) to extract the field amplitude and phase profile of each BSV pulse, by Fourier analysis of the interference rings between the BSV and a coherent reference with different phase-front curvature. The concentric ring interference fringes are robust against pointing mismatch and drift, thereby simplifying the analysis. The measured distribution has two phase peaks separated by $\pi$ radians. The rings sweep the delay between the two pulses, so a single frame can capture the temporal structure of the BSV field, even when it is composed of several temporal modes.

papers.title: Spin-dependent fermion potentials from mixed tensor couplings of massive spin-1 and spin-2 bosons
papers.abstract: Searches for weak spin-dependent forces are commonly interpreted in terms of a basis of sixteen rotationally invariant two-fermion potentials. We derive finite-range coordinate-space potentials generated by a massive spin-1 boson with vector, axial-vector, tensor, and pseudotensor couplings to Dirac fermions. In addition to the familiar vector--vector, vector--axial-vector, and axial-vector--axial-vector interactions, we obtain the mixed vector--tensor, vector--pseudotensor, axial-vector--tensor, and axial-vector--pseudotensor potentials, together with tensor--tensor, tensor--pseudotensor, and pseudotensor--pseudotensor terms. We retain the contact terms needed in atomic-scale applications and give compact expressions that include both orderings of inequivalent fermion vertices. We then extend the analysis to a massive spin-2 mediator described by a symmetric Fierz--Pauli field. Besides the conventional coupling to the conserved fermion energy--momentum tensor, we consider a symmetric axial-tensor current. Its nonconservation for massive fermions makes the longitudinal spin-2 helicities contribute to axial-tensor--axial-tensor exchange. The leading minimal spin-2 interactions are either P,T even or P odd and T evenl. Heavy-mediator contact limits and the distinction between the M-->0 massive-spin-2 limit and a genuine massless graviton are also discussed. We map the resulting interactions onto the sixteen-potential Dobrescu--Mocioiu basis and use this mapping to translate existing experimental constraints into numerical limits on spin-1 and spin-2 coupling products in the small- and large-mediator-mass regimes, together with representative limits at finite mediator masses. The derived relations between the boson-exchange coupling constants and the coefficients of the basis potentials also allow published exclusion curves to be rescaled to arbitrary mediator masses.

papers.title: Electron Scattering with ASTRA: Helium and Molecular Hydrogen
papers.abstract: We present an implementation of electron-impact scattering in \ASTRA{}~(AttoSecond TRAnsitions)~[J. M. Randazzo {\it et al.}, Phys. Rev. Research {\bf 5}, 043115 (2023)], a general close-coupling method for the molecular electronic continuum based on transition density matrices and already employed for molecular photoionization. The scattering states are obtained with a pole-free Galerkin method with variational surface matching, which yields the scattering matrix and, from it, the elastic and electronically inelastic integral cross sections and the molecular-frame differential cross sections. For helium, \ASTRA{} reproduces elastic and inelastic cross sections over a broad energy range, resolves the $\mathrm{He}^{-}(1s2s^2\,{}^2S^e)$ Feshbach resonance in both energy and angle, and reproduces the interference features in the angular distributions for $1s^2\to1s 2\ell$ excitations observed experimentally. For molecular hydrogen, the elastic and inelastic cross sections closely reproduce the benchmark results obtained with \UKRmolplus{} for the same close-coupling expansion. We also report orientation-resolved, three-dimensional molecular-frame angular distributions for state-resolved electron-impact excitation, which are shown to depend strongly on the molecular orientation. These results validate the method in view of its application to larger molecular targets.
